summary: Created a LUKS2-encrypted volume on node1 (file-backed at /root/secure.img, unlocked via a root-only random keyfile in /etc/cryptsetup-keys.d/secure.key, XFS filesystem) that automatically unlocks via /etc/crypttab and mounts at /srv/secure via /etc/fstab at boot without any interactive passphrase. Verified this survives a full node reboot: boot identity changed from deef5424-198c-4c8e-95f2-5cd8c8ea3f8d to 9083360a-2982-450d-8966-e208225253f4, and post-reboot the systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service was active, /srv/secure was mounted from /dev/mapper/secure, and previously written test data (hello encrypted) was intact.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/disk layout (CentOS Stream 10, single root disk, no spare block device)
Created a 2GiB backing file /root/secure.img and a 512-byte random keyfile /etc/cryptsetup-keys.d/secure.key (mode 600)
Ran cryptsetup luksFormat (LUKS2, aes-xts-plain64) on the backing file using the keyfile
Opened the LUKS volume as /dev/mapper/secure and formatted it with XFS
Added /etc/crypttab entry ('secure /root/secure.img /etc/cryptsetup-keys.d/secure.key luks') and /etc/fstab entry (UUID=... /srv/secure xfs defaults 0 2)
Reloaded systemd and validated systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service auto-unlocks the volume, then mounted with mount -a and wrote a test file
Captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, uptime, mount state, test file contents, cryptsetup status)
Triggered a background-delayed systemctl reboot on node1 so the exec call could return before disconnection
Polled node1 until it reconnected after the reboot
Verified boot_id changed (proof of actual restart) and confirmed systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service active, /srv/secure mounted, and test data intact post-reboot

evidence.requirement: Encrypted volume created and mounted at /srv/secure
evidence.summary: LUKS2 luksFormat succeeded, XFS filesystem created on /dev/mapper/secure, blkid confirms UUID, and mount -a mounts /dev/mapper/secure at /srv/secure with a test file written

evidence.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts automatically at boot (no manual intervention)
evidence.summary: crypttab keyfile entry and fstab mount entry configured; systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service starts and unlocks the volume automatically using only the on-disk keyfile, no interactive passphrase

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id deef5424-198c-4c8e-95f2-5cd8c8ea3f8d, active systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service, /srv/secure mounted, and test file content readable prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: reboot acknowledgement returns before disconnect
evidence.summary: Reboot triggered via backgrounded delayed systemctl reboot; exec call returned 'triggered' immediately before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: node restarted one at a time, polled until available
evidence.summary: Connection failures during reboot window followed by successful reconnection once node1 came back up

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: changed boot identity proves an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from deef5424-198c-4c8e-95f2-5cd8c8ea3f8d to 9083360a-2982-450d-8966-e208225253f4, and uptime -s shows a new boot time (2026-09-04 23:10:15)

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: post-restart proof of recovered required service and data
evidence.summary: After reboot, systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service is active, /srv/secure is mounted from /dev/mapper/secure, and the previously written test file content ('hello encrypted') is intact, all without any manual unlock/mount action
